venue.name: Shaw Centre for the Salish Sea
venue.description: The Shaw Centre for the Salish Sea is a not for profit aquarium and learning centre on the Sidney waterfront, with over 3,500 animals from 160 Salish Sea species, a marine mammal exhibit including a rare orca skeleton, and a collection of Coast Salish art. There is an open touch pool and a dedicated classroom the Centre calls Ocean's Heartbeat. Facilitated school programs run from October to June for preschool through grade 12 at a published per student rate, and self guided group visits at a reduced rate are available for groups of 12 or more. Food and drink may not be eaten inside the building, so lunch happens outside on Beacon Park.

facility_notes.lunch_space: We do not have space in our Centre to consume snacks or lunch. The aquarium is situated on Beacon Park by the Sidney waterfront and there are a number of benches as well as a large lawn area. Picnic tables can also be found between Beacon Wharf and the fishing pier, just a couple of minutes' walk from the aquarium. You are able to leave the Centre and re-enter.
facility_notes.rain_backup: There is a large grassy area outside of the facility with a covered band shell in case of inclement weather. The aquarium itself is indoors.
facility_notes.stroller_accessible: Strollers are permitted throughout the aquarium. We just ask that you are mindful of other visitors when you park and be sure not to obstruct doorways or exhibit views.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: The Centre strives to be accessible to all. A wheelchair is available free of charge on a first come-first served basis. Please ask at our admissions desk. The behind the scenes tour is the exception and cannot be done with a mobility device.
facility_notes.bus_parking: For bus arrivals, students can be dropped off at the entrance but unfortunately there is no bus parking nearby. Bus parking is located at Tulista Park (9565 Fifth Street) and the Mary Winspear Centre (2243 Beacon Avenue). Free two hour parking in the underground lot is limited to vehicles under 6'6" in height.

venue.nearby_park: Beacon Park, on the Sidney waterfront beside the Centre
restrictions: Food or drink may not be consumed inside the aquarium
For the safety of our animals and visitors, only trained service dogs are permitted in the aquarium
Smoking is prohibited inside the building and within 7m of doorways, this includes e-cigarettes
Siblings of students are unable to participate in the program without prior approval
Youth 13 years and over may visit the Centre without an accompanying adult. All children under this age must be accompanied by someone over the age of 13
Please turn off your flash when taking photos inside the aquarium, and do not use tripods or monopods
venue.hours_notes: Open daily 10:00 to 16:30, with last entry 30 minutes before closing. Tickets are available on entry and no booking is needed for a family visit, but groups of 12 or more must book in advance.
venue.seasonal_notes: Facilitated school programs run October to June, and the school programs page says the Centre is closed on Wednesdays during the school year. Published closures include annual maintenance in February, January 1, September 30, November 11 and December 24 to 26. The Centre stays open on other statutory holidays and through spring break.

programs.name: Adventures of a Crab
programs.description: A facilitated program for preschool and kindergarten groups, with a minimum age of 3. Children meet a hermit crab looking for a new home and learn about food, protection and shelter through storytelling, games and hands-on, hands-wet learning. Live animal ambassadors are included. It runs entirely in the Ocean's Heartbeat classroom rather than out in the galleries, so plan extra time either side if you want the children to see the tanks and the touch pool.
programs.what_children_do: Sit together in the classroom for a story about a hermit crab looking for a new shell, play games about food and shelter, and get their hands wet meeting live animals the educator brings out. It is 45 minutes in one room, not a walk around the aquarium.
programs.our_note: This is the only program that takes under fives, and it caps at 20 children. Because it all happens in the classroom, book time before or after to walk the galleries and the touch pool, otherwise the children will not see the aquarium at all.
programs.practical_summary: Indoors the whole time and 45 minutes long, with one free teacher and a free chaperone for every 5 children. There is nowhere inside to eat, so lunch is on the lawn at Beacon Park, and washrooms are not mentioned on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: The minimum charge is the price of 15 students, so a group smaller than 15 still pays for 15.
programs.payment_timing: Full payment is expected upon arrival. Payment can be made by cash, debit or credit card. They cannot provide an invoice in advance of your visit.

programs.name: Pod Squad
programs.description: A facilitated program for kindergarten to grade 2 about marine mammals, focused on the killer whale. Students investigate communication, echolocation and photo-identification, and talk about why the resident killer whales are endangered and how people can protect them. It takes place entirely in the Ocean's Heartbeat classroom.
programs.what_children_do: Work in the classroom with the educator on how killer whales find each other and find food, trying out echolocation and matching whales by their markings in photographs.
programs.our_note: It is a classroom hour with no gallery time built in, so add half an hour before or after if you want the children to see the tanks. Best for a class that is already comfortable sitting and listening in a group.
programs.practical_summary: One hour indoors, up to 22 children, one free teacher and a free chaperone for every 5. Lunch has to happen outside on the park lawn and washrooms are not mentioned on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: The minimum charge is the price of 15 students, so a group smaller than 15 still pays for 15.
programs.payment_timing: Full payment is expected upon arrival. Payment can be made by cash, debit or credit card. They cannot provide an invoice in advance of your visit.

programs.name: Feeding Frenzy
programs.description: A facilitated program for kindergarten to grade 2 about how Salish Sea animals eat. Students work out what seastars eat and how a jelly catches its food, exploring feeding behaviours through hands-on learning and interactive activities set up as a mystery to solve.
programs.what_children_do: Handle materials and work through clues with the educator to figure out which animal has which kind of mouth and how each one catches its food.
programs.our_note: A good fit for a class that likes a puzzle to solve rather than a talk to listen to. Ask when you book whether this one uses the touch pool, since the site does not say.
programs.practical_summary: One hour indoors, up to 22 children, with one free teacher and a free chaperone for every 5. There is no room inside to eat lunch and washrooms are not mentioned on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: The minimum charge is the price of 15 students, so a group smaller than 15 still pays for 15.
programs.payment_timing: Full payment is expected upon arrival. Payment can be made by cash, debit or credit card. They cannot provide an invoice in advance of your visit.

programs.name: Salish Sea Safari
programs.description: A facilitated program for grades 3 to 5. Students observe and have hands-on experiences with marine life across three habitats, eelgrass meadows, rocky shores and the open water, and look at how the animals and their habitats connect to each other. Conservation concerns affecting those habitats are discussed.
programs.what_children_do: Move between three habitat areas with the educator, looking closely at live animals and handling what they are allowed to handle, then talk about which animal belongs where and why.
programs.our_note: This is the one that gets the children out among the exhibits rather than sitting in the classroom. It runs 75 minutes, which is long for a group that tires standing up, so think about where a rest fits.
programs.practical_summary: Seventy five minutes indoors, up to 28 children, one free teacher and a free chaperone for every 5. Lunch is outside on the park lawn and washrooms are not mentioned on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: The minimum charge is the price of 15 students, so a group smaller than 15 still pays for 15.
programs.payment_timing: Full payment is expected upon arrival. Payment can be made by cash, debit or credit card. They cannot provide an invoice in advance of your visit.

programs.name: Killer Whale Tales
programs.description: A facilitated program for grades 3 to 5 taking an in depth look at how endangered Southern resident killer whales, people and the environment are connected. Students explore killer whale biology, behaviour and conservation through hands-on activities involving echolocation, photo-identification and communication.
programs.what_children_do: Work through hands-on activities with the educator on how killer whales communicate and find food, and identify individual whales from photographs of their markings.
programs.our_note: Very close in content to Marine Mammal Stewards, which is the same material pitched at grades 6 to 8, so pick by the age of your class rather than the title. Ask whether it includes gallery time when you book.
programs.practical_summary: Seventy five minutes indoors, up to 28 children, one free teacher and a free chaperone for every 5. There is nowhere inside to eat and washrooms are not mentioned on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: The minimum charge is the price of 15 students, so a group smaller than 15 still pays for 15.
programs.payment_timing: Full payment is expected upon arrival. Payment can be made by cash, debit or credit card. They cannot provide an invoice in advance of your visit.

programs.name: Marine Mammal Stewards
programs.description: A facilitated program for grades 6 to 8 investigating how endangered Southern resident killer whales interact with their environment and what they need to survive. Students explore killer whale biology, behaviour and conservation through hands-on activities involving echolocation, photo-identification and communication.
programs.what_children_do: Take part in hands-on activities on echolocation and whale identification, and discuss what the resident whales need from their environment and what is going wrong for them.
programs.our_note: The touch pool is open, so leave time either side to use it. The Centre notes that siblings of students cannot join a program without asking first, which catches out mixed age groups.
programs.practical_summary: Seventy five minutes indoors, up to 28 students, one free teacher and a free chaperone for every 5. Lunch is outside on the park lawn and washrooms are not mentioned on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: The minimum charge is the price of 15 students, so a group smaller than 15 still pays for 15.
programs.payment_timing: Full payment is expected upon arrival. Payment can be made by cash, debit or credit card. They cannot provide an invoice in advance of your visit.

programs.name: Marine Invertebrate Zoology
programs.description: A facilitated program for grades 9 to 12 taking an in depth look at four phyla using examples from the Salish Sea. Living and preserved specimens show the characteristics and adaptations of Cnidaria, Mollusca, Arthropoda and Echinodermata. The program includes hands-wet time at the touch pool.
programs.what_children_do: Examine living and preserved specimens up close, compare the four groups, and spend part of the session with hands in the touch pool.
programs.our_note: The free chaperone rate drops to one adult per 10 students at this age, so budget for more paying adults than a younger class would need.
programs.practical_summary: Ninety minutes indoors, up to 28 students, one free teacher and a free chaperone for every 10. There is nowhere inside to eat and washrooms are not mentioned on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: The minimum charge is the price of 15 students, so a group smaller than 15 still pays for 15.
programs.payment_timing: Full payment is expected upon arrival. Payment can be made by cash, debit or credit card. They cannot provide an invoice in advance of your visit.

programs.name: Art in the Aquarium
programs.description: A session for grades 9 to 12 in which students draw, sketch or paint among the habitats, taking their subject from the colours and shapes of Salish Sea life. The Centre states that supplies and instruction are not included, so the teacher brings the materials and leads the work. Length is 1 hour 30 minutes and flexible.
programs.what_children_do: Sit or stand in front of the tanks with their own paper and materials and draw the animals and habitats in front of them.
programs.our_note: Supplies and instruction are not included, so this is really studio time in a beautiful room rather than a taught class. Email their Director of Learning before you commit, because the page says to.
programs.practical_summary: Ninety minutes indoors and flexible in length, up to 28 students, one free teacher and a free chaperone for every 10. Bring your own art materials. There is nowhere inside to eat and washrooms are not mentioned on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: The minimum charge is the price of 15 students, so a group smaller than 15 still pays for 15. Art supplies and instruction are not included.
programs.payment_timing: Full payment is expected upon arrival. Payment can be made by cash, debit or credit card. They cannot provide an invoice in advance of your visit.

programs.name: Self guided group visit
programs.description: Groups of 12 or more paying guests get a reduced admission rate and lead themselves around the aquarium with no guide or tour. Children aged 4 to 12 are $8.00 plus tax, youth 13 to 18 are $11.25, adults 19 to 64 are $15.50, seniors are $13.25 and children 3 and under are free. One adult goes free for every 10 paying guests. Classes are welcome to come this way and a range of printable scavenger hunts is available on request or from the website. Admission lasts the whole day so a group can leave and come back.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the galleries at their own pace looking into the tanks, stop at the touch pool, and work through a scavenger hunt sheet if the group brings one.
programs.our_note: The rate and the free adult allowance are different from the school program ones, so do not mix the two up when you budget. Groups are asked to arrive together at the booked time and may be told to wait outside, so dress the children for standing in the weather.
programs.practical_summary: About an hour indoors and self led, minimum 12 paying guests, with one free adult for every 10. There is nowhere inside to eat, lunch is on the park lawn outside, and washrooms are not mentioned on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: The child rate is for ages 4 to 12. Youth 13 to 18 are $11.25 plus tax, seniors 65 and over are $13.25 plus tax, and children 3 and under are free. The Centre reserves the right to limit group size or ask a group to split and stagger entry.
programs.payment_timing: Admission costs are payable in person on arrival by cash, debit or credit card.

programs.name: Behind the Scenes Aquarium Tour
programs.description: A 45 minute tour led by an aquarist through the working areas visitors do not normally see, including the sculpin nursery, the jellyfish culture area and the water systems. It costs regular admission plus $17 plus tax per person, takes 6 people maximum and 2 minimum, and runs Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday at 11:30 and 14:00. Other days and times may be possible for groups of 4 or more with at least 7 days notice. Guests must be at least 8 years old and anyone under 13 needs an adult with them.
programs.what_children_do: Follow an aquarist through back rooms and up and down stairs, looking at tanks of young fish, the jellyfish setup and the pumps and pipes that keep the aquarium running.
programs.our_note: Six people maximum makes this a treat for a handful of children rather than a class outing. The Centre says plainly it does not suit anyone with a seafood allergy, noise sensitivity or a mobility device, and everyone has to sign a waiver at check in.
programs.practical_summary: Forty five minutes on top of a regular visit, for 2 to 6 people aged 8 and up, and it costs admission plus $17 each plus tax. It involves stairs, uneven floors, narrow spaces and loud machinery, so it is not step free and not quiet.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $17 is per person and sits on top of regular admission, which is $9.50 for a child aged 4 to 12 and $19.50 for an adult, both plus GST. Members get 10 percent off.
programs.cancellation_note: The Centre reserves the right to cancel the tour with limited notice due to emergency events, which may include rare instances related to animal welfare or operational concerns. A full refund for the tour applies in that case.
programs.evidence: Cost is Regular Admission plus $17+tax (per person)
